description.value: An event-related BOLD fMRI study of healthy volunteers examining neural correlates of using distancing to regulate emotional responses to negative social situations, with a fully crossed instruction-by-picture-valence design.

spans.text: To our knowledge, this study is the first to focus specifically on the use of distancing to regulate responses to aversive social cues employing an event-related fMRI design.

value: we expected that carrying out reappraisal of social-emotional cues by distancing would involve the recruitment of prefrontal and cingulate systems previously implicated in the top–down cognitive control of limbic, attentional and primary sensory regions.

we expected to observe activity in medial frontal and medial parietal regions associated with self-referential processing and perspective-taking, as well as prefrontal and parietal regions implicated in the top–down control of attention

we expected that the selective presentation of aversive social-emotional cues would activate systems associated with processing aversive stimuli, such as the amygdala, as well as regions implicated in processing the relevance of social cues, such as the superior temporal sulcus
we expected amygdala activity to be modulated by engagement of the distancing strategy

description.value: A 2 × 2 event-related design crossed instruction type (look versus distance) with stimulus type (negative versus neutral).

spans.text: In the 2 × 2 design, BOLD fMRI scans were obtained as subjects viewed negative and neutral images while carrying out instructions either to downregulate their emotional reactions using the reappraisal by distancing strategy (distance condition) or to simply allow themselves to look at the pictures without trying to affect their response (look condition).

BOLD fMRI
MRI scanning was performed using a Siemens 3.0 T Allegra scanner.

BOLD images were obtained with a gradient echoplanar (GE-EPI) sequence with the following protocol: 42 axial slices, 2.5 mm thick, skip = 0.825 mm, TR = 3 s, TE = 27 ms, Flip angle = 84°, FOV = 21 cm, matrix = 64 × 64.
